message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "# This workflow will build a Java project with Gradle
# For more information see: https://help.github.com/actions/language-and-framework-guides/building-and-testing-java-with-gradle

name: Java CI with Gradle

on:
  push:
    branches: [ 1.16.x ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ 1.16.x ]

jobs:
  build:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Set up JDK 1.8
      uses: actions/setup-java@v1
      with:
        java-version: 1.8
    - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
      run: chmod +x gradlew
    - name: Cache Gradle dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.gradle/caches
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('**/*.gradle*', '**/gradle-wrapper.properties') }}
    - name: Build with Gradle
      run: ./gradlew build",
  "rationale": "The workflow is a Gradle-based Java build with no existing dependency cache. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern and the measured Gradle experiment (batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200, ~20.4% elapsed savings) support adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.gradle/caches keyed on Gradle files and the wrapper properties. This preserves the existing build/test coverage (./gradlew build still runs), adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing, deployment, or new network access beyond the existing build, and is a minimal, unrelated-change-free insertion before the build step.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-interactive-three--91c08fe132959200", "pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE"]
}
